private_note: I can't know my group or even estimate the odds, and this choice binds me for a generation with no second chance. So I rank plans by how well I'd do in the worst case. Hazel guarantees 41, the highest floor available. Birch (36) and Alder (32) come next. Today is a failed convention with a floor of 22. Cedar's floor of 15 is the only outcome I'd find truly ruinous, and I'll block it.
statement: Fellow delegates, every one of us is in the same position. None of us knows which fifth we will wake up in, and none of us can put odds on it. The decision is final and lasts a generation. When you can't calculate your chances and can't undo the choice, the sensible thing is to make sure that the worst place you might land is still a decent one. Hazel does that better than any other plan: the lowest fifth gets 41, nearly double today's 22, and no plan can sustainably raise it higher. Cedar gambles on landing at the top, but if any of us is in the bottom fifth we get 15. Ask yourself whether you would accept that bet blind. My ranking is Hazel, then Birch, then Alder. I would rather see us agree on a high floor than fail and keep today's arrangements. I am open to Birch or Alder if Hazel can't reach nine votes.
